claim: hyperunix.find returns no file name or path for any row: the capability value holds anonymous stat records (mode, size, uid, gid, nlink, mtime, ctime, st-dev, st-ino plus base64 device/inode identity keys), so an agent cannot learn WHICH files matched. The names exist natively (hx.fs/entry-name on edge-claim frames) and are dropped because the vendored SDK's QueryResult.rows keeps node-claims only and the provider returns resultToJson(native) unchanged.
evidence: node probes/providers/h01-hx-native-find.mjs '[["hx.fs/regular-file","src"]]' (the pin's dist nativeHyperUnixFind, real hx 0.1.0) -> ok, bytes 150439, rows 135; python scan of probes/providers/h01-hx-find-src.json: '.ts' occurs 0 times in the whole payload, plain/decoded hits for index.ts / capability-registry / workbench / providers = 0, row keys = [attributes, element, identities, kinds, supports]. Control: `hx --workspace $PIN find --kind hx.fs/regular-file src/workbench/providers --best-effort --hxs` (probes/providers/hx-find-providers.hxs) carries 4 edge-claim frames whose hx.fs/entry-name decodes to forge.ts, furnace.ts, hyperunix.ts, reactivefiber.ts. Real Pi tool path (probes/providers/vt/node-e2e.log, case s1b-naive): {rowsLength:6, answerCount:3, anyNameField:false} on a 3-file src. Code: src/workbench/providers/hyperunix.ts:25,44 (resultToJson); node_modules/@hyperunix/sdk/dist/result.d.ts:4 ('One node-claim body ... the row type of the typed reads').
cost: Every agent or script that calls hyperunix.find to enumerate files (the only use the worked example in docs/workbench/19-worked-examples.md:87-95 shows): each call spends 12-150 KB and yields nothing addressable; the agent falls back to Bash find/ls.
cureHint: Project the answer set with names in the provider: read the edge-claims' hx.fs/entry-name (or the hx-results answer frames) into a compact rows:[{path, kind}] beside the native source; if that needs SDK support, state in the descriptor that rows carry no names.

claim: hyperunix.find's source.rows is the observation proof graph, not the answer set: it is identical for every kind asked. An agent that reads rows (or rows.length) gets a wrong answer for every query; only coverage_summary.answer_count reflects the match count, and nothing in the descriptor or docs says so.
evidence: node probes/providers/h02-registry.mjs (index.ts registryFor path: new CapabilityRegistry() + registerNativeProviders) on the pin's src (124 files, 6 dirs): kind hx.fs/regular-file -> rows 135, answer_count 124; kind hx.fs/directory -> rows 135, answer_count 5; kind hx.fs/symlink -> rows 135, answer_count 0 (probes/providers/h02-run1.out). Real Pi tool + workflow_observe run (probes/providers/vt/observe.log): {symAnswer:0, symRows:3}. docs/workbench/19-worked-examples.md:95 says 'The native result can be incomplete even when files are returned', which reads rows as files.
cost: Any agent using the capability for a count, an existence check or a listing: a symlink query over a tree with none returns 135 rows; absence checks read as presence. Silent wrong answers, every call.
cureHint: Return an explicit answers array (the hx answer frames / answer-coverage projection) and move the proof graph under a separately named key; until then put 'rows are proof-graph nodes; read coverage_summary.answer_count' in the descriptor description and the worked example.

claim: hyperunix.find has no limit, cursor, projection or exclusion input and costs about 1 KB per node plus 8-10 KB of coverage overhead, so it overruns every output bound on ordinary directories: the curated Claude tool (32 KB) rejects the capability's own default root src and any directory above roughly 25 entries; node() (256 KB registry bound) rejects test/; root '.' dies at the SDK's 8 MiB stream limit. The rejection is category 'validation' with text 'Payload exceeds N bytes.', which blames the caller's input and names no way to narrow.
evidence: Real MCP client against the pin's createCuratedTools (probes/providers/h03-curated.mjs, output probes/providers/h03-run2.out): capability_invoke hyperunix.find root src -> isError, {"kind":"rejected","category":"validation","diagnostic":"Payload exceeds 32768 bytes."}; root src/workbench -> same; src/workflow (16 files) -> 23153 bytes; src/ui (11 files) -> 18513; src/workbench/providers (4 files) -> 12087. Registry path (probes/providers/h02-run1.out): root test (937 files) -> category validation 'Payload exceeds 262144 bytes.'; root docs (105 files) -> 127366 bytes. Root '.' -> 'Capability hyperunix.find failed: SDK_PROTOCOL_LIMIT: output_bytes exceeded 8388608 (observed 8454144)' after 4.6-14.2 s (probes/providers/h01-run2.out, h03-run2.out). Schema: src/workbench/providers/hyperunix.ts:14 (kind, root only).
cost: Claude-role agents on every non-trivial directory (hard failure); script authors on any tree above ~230 entries; each failed attempt still pays the full hx walk (0.3-14 s).
cureHint: Add limit + cursor (and a names-only projection) to the input schema and page the result under the bound; when a bound is hit, return a typed partial with nextCursor instead of a validation rejection, or at least say 'output exceeded N bytes; narrow root'.

claim: The Pi-side model (the one that writes node() scripts) has no way to read any provider's input schema. workbench_catalog rows omit inputSchema, and workflow_inspect - the only Pi tool that would show one - refuses all four registered capabilities with inspect-not-advertised even when every grant is present, because every native descriptor declares supportedModes ['invoke'] only. The Claude-role side does have capability_contract; the orchestrating model does not.
evidence: Real extension booted with discover:* + inspect:* grants for all four ids (probes/providers/vt/node-e2e.probe.test.ts case S7, log probes/providers/vt/node-e2e.log): workbench_catalog -> rows of {id, version, description, effectClass, modes, contractSource}; workflow_inspect {target, view:'schema'} for forge.gate.status, hyperunix.find, furnace.run.inspect and reactivefiber.render.preview -> each {"ok":false,"error":{"code":"unavailable","reason":"inspect-not-advertised","message":"The capability does not advertise an inspect mode."}}. For hyperunix.find the definition, schema and operations views all refuse the same way (probes/providers/h04-run1.out). Census (probes/providers/census.sh -> census.out): 8 registry.register sites in src, all under src/workbench/providers/, each with supportedModes ['invoke'] (hx exports roster in probes/providers/hx-exports-*.out, coverage partial HX-COV-004). docs/workbench/06-capability-registry.md:47 promises 'Allow on-demand capability contract retrieval' on the Pi side and :55 'For native operations with a Run/operation ID, advertise independent inspect/observe'. No open bead found (literal + regex scan of .beads/issues.jsonl and both archives, 2689 rows).
cost: Every orchestrating agent in Workbench mode: it must guess input keys (kind/root, model/task, view/taskId, runId) or read source; workflow_inspect is a registered tool that can only refuse on the shipped capability set.
cureHint: Include inputSchema (or a schema view gated on discover:<id>) in the catalog/inspect reply for invoke-only capabilities; the descriptor is static metadata and needs no provider inspect().

claim: The hyperunix.find provider discards the native HX diagnostic on a refused query. A mistyped kind reaches the agent as 'Capability hyperunix.find failed: hx exited unsuccessfully with status 2' in category transport, while hx itself returned HX-TYPE-UNKNOWN-KIND with a remediation that names the fix. The SDK error the provider lets fall through already carries that diagnostic.
evidence: Registry path (probes/providers/h02-run1.out): {kind:'regular-file', root:'src'} -> {category:'transport', message:'Capability hyperunix.find failed: hx exited unsuccessfully with status 2'}; real Pi tool path (probes/providers/vt/node-e2e.log s2-bad-kind): <status>Error: Capability hyperunix.find failed: hx exited unsuccessfully with status 2</status>; root '' gives the same message through the registry, and kind hx.js/function the same SDK failure through the provider function (probes/providers/h01-run2.out). Native control: `hx --workspace $PIN find --kind regular-file src --best-effort` -> exit 2, {"code":"HX-TYPE-UNKNOWN-KIND", remediation.action:"spell a kind one of the 13 admitted bundles declares or aliases: 'hx schema aliases' ... use 'hx find --kind hx.fs/regular-file' for files"} (probes/providers/hx-badkind.err). probes/providers/h08-run.out: the thrown ProcessFailureError has result.exitCode 2 and result.diagnostics[0].code HX-TYPE-UNKNOWN-KIND with the remediation. Code: src/workbench/providers/hyperunix.ts:42-45 (no catch), src/workbench/capability-registry.ts:437 (non-CapabilityError -> transport).
cost: Any agent that guesses a kind (the schema gives no vocabulary): it cannot self-correct and 'transport' invites a blind retry; exit class 2 is a usage error.
cureHint: Catch the SDK ProcessFailureError in the provider: map exit class 2 to category validation and put diagnostics[0].code plus remediation.action in the message.

claim: The curated Claude capability tools cut every rejection diagnostic to 100 bytes, which removes the informative tail of most real messages (absolute paths consume the budget) and can end mid-token.

claim: workbench.reactivefiberWorkspaceRoot is compared to rf's reported root by exact string, so a symlinked path or a trailing slash - both of which settings validation admits and rf itself renders successfully - makes every preview fail with 'RF preview returned an unrecognized or contradictory envelope.' Correcting the setting has no effect until Pi restarts, because the per-workspace registry caches the provider with the old root, and nothing says so.
evidence: Real extension (probes/providers/vt/rf-root-setting.probe.test.ts, log vt/rf-root-setting.log): setting '<rfws>/' boots, run r1 -> status error 'RF preview returned an unrecognized or contradictory envelope.'; .pi/subagents.json rewritten to '<rfws>' in the same session, run r2 -> the same error. Harness (probes/providers/h02-run-rf-symlink.out, h02-run-rf-slash.out): symlink root and trailing-slash root -> category transport, same text, while `rf --workspace <symlink> context render ... --json` -> ok:true with workspace.root = the real path. Code: src/workbench/providers/reactivefiber.ts:65 (root !== workspaceRoot), src/settings.ts:374-381 and :418 (isCleanAbsolutePath only), src/index.ts:2484-2500 (registries Map, setting read once).
cost: Operators configuring a swarm RF workspace (home directories are commonly symlinked; on this host `ls -ld /home/jehallad` -> '/home/jehallad -> /local/home/jehallad', probes/providers/census.out): total, unexplained failure of the RF capability, then a second trap when the fix does not take.
cureHint: Canonicalise the setting with realpath at registration (as the scope already is) or compare realpaths; name the mismatch in the error; rebuild the registry entry when the setting changes.

claim: Provider input schemas are bare and hide a default: no property has a description, example, enum or default. hyperunix.find's kind is an open string with no pointer to the kind vocabulary, and the native registration silently substitutes root 'src' when root is omitted, so in a workspace without src/ a no-root query returns an 'incomplete' one-row answer about a path the caller never named.

No-root call in a workspace with no src (the scratch rf workspace): ok:true, rows 1 (kinds ['hx.fs/namespace']), execution_status.kind 'incomplete', diagnostic '.../rf-ws/src names no entry (trace outcome Missing, existence Unknown)' (probes/providers/h02-hx-nosrc.json). Code: src/workbench/providers/hyperunix.ts:50 (`root??"src"`), :14. The injected-reader registration (:16-27) applies no default, so the two registrations of one id differ.
cost: Agents on any repository that is not laid out as src/ (monorepos, Python, Go): a plausible call returns a confusing non-answer; every agent must discover the kind vocabulary by failing.
cureHint: Add description, examples (hx.fs/regular-file) and default to the schema properties; require root explicitly or state the default in the contract; point at `hx schema list` for kinds.

claim: Authorization refusals never name the missing grant, and the Claude-role journey needs three separate grants per capability (discover:<id>, invoke:<id> and the producer permission) on top of role exposure. With any one missing the agent sees 'Claude capability permission denied.' or an empty discover list, indistinguishable from 'nothing is installed'. The same producer grant that makes node() work leaves the Claude tools fully denied.

(s5). Unknown id through the Claude tool -> 'Claude capability permission denied.' rather than unknown capability (probes/providers/h03-run2.out). Contrast: src/workbench/claude-evidence.ts:89 names its grant. Docs: one sentence at docs/workflows.md:464; no shipped .pi/subagents.json example pairs roles.<name>.capabilities with the three grants (grep of README.md, docs/workflows.md, docs/workbench/*.md).
cost: Operators wiring a Claude role to a provider: trial and error over three grant strings with an identical denial each time; agents handed the tools with a missing discover grant hit an empty list and stop.
cureHint: Name the missing grant in the refusal (the operator already owns the grant list), and ship one worked settings block in docs/workbench/19.

claim: A missing producer binary surfaces four different ways across the four providers, and nothing warns before invocation: three use category transport and one unavailable; only Furnace says ENOENT; Forge reports a closed connection; RF does not name rf. Discovery still lists all four capabilities, the extension has no preflight or doctor surface, and the shipped docs say only 'Install those executables independently'.

Same PATH, capability_discover still returns all four (probes/providers/h03-run-nobin-discover.out). Absence surfaces: grep of src for doctor|healthcheck -> 0 hits (probes/providers/census.out; the one 'preflight' in src is furnace-hosted contract decoding); vendor/README.md:3 is the only install statement; no minimum versions anywhere in README.md, docs/workflows.md, docs/workbench/17.
cost: Operators on a fresh install and agents on any host missing one tool: the failure appears mid-workflow, and 'transport' cannot be told from a transient fault.
cureHint: Use category unavailable with one sentence shape ('<tool> executable not found on PATH') in all four providers, and add a preflight (settings menu row or a workbench doctor reply) that reports each binary's presence and version.

claim: The registry's default 30 s deadline fires before the RF provider's own 60 s bound, so that bound and its 'RF preview exceeded the execution deadline.' message are unreachable under the host's registry (reproduced). By code read only (SUPPORTED, not run): hyperunix.find's 30 s wall bound with a 60 s SDK timeout races the same 30 s cut, so a slow query would be reported as a registry timeout instead of HX's bounded partial answer.
evidence: A fake rf that sleeps 45 s first on PATH, invoked through the default registry (probes/providers/h05-rf-deadline.mjs, output h05b-run.out): {registryDefaultDeadlineMs:30000, ms:30029, category:'transport', message:'Capability reactivefiber.render.preview exceeded its deadline of 30000ms.'}. Code: src/workbench/capability-registry.ts:62 (CAPABILITY_DEADLINE_MS 30_000), src/index.ts:2490 (new CapabilityRegistry() with no limits), src/workbench/providers/reactivefiber.ts:157,174 (60_000), src/workbench/providers/hyperunix.ts:21,42 (wall '30s', timeoutMs 60_000). Injected variants registerHyperUnixFind / registerForgeGateStatus / registerFurnaceRunInspect / registerReactiveFiberRender: 0 src call sites, referenced by 41 / 17 / 20 / 64 test files; native variants: 2 src call sites each, 9 / 8 / 4 / 56 test files (probes/providers/census.out; hx exports roster probes/providers/hx-exports-*.out, 24 bindings, coverage partial).
